quotes.text: You can only configure [Adaptive Pricing](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing.md) and the Currency Selector Element when using Elements with the [Checkout Sessions API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart.md).
To display currency options, you must complete the following steps:
Set [adaptivePricing.allowed](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing.md?payment-ui=embedded-components#mark-integration-ready) to `true` in the Checkout Session.

Use an integration or price currency that’s [eligible for settlement](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing.md?payment-ui=embedded-components#restrictions) by the merchant of record.
You must render the Currency Selector Element in your use of Adaptive Pricing with Elements.

old_evidence.text: [Adaptive Pricing](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing.md) and the Currency Selector Element are only available when using Elements with the [Checkout Sessions API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart-checkout-sessions.md).
You must render the Currency Selector Element in your use of Adaptive Pricing with Elements.
Add the Currency Selector near where payment details are entered, ideally directly above the Payment Element, since the selected currency might affect available payment methods.

findings: New raw lines 17-21 add explicit display prerequisites absent from old raw: enable Adaptive Pricing, set `adaptivePricing.allowed` true in the Checkout Session, and use an integration or price currency eligible for settlement by the merchant of record. Current source covers Checkout Sessions restriction and initialization but omits these prerequisites; add them with the Session scope and merchant-of-record qualification.

New raw line 13 restates the old Checkout Sessions API restriction at old raw line 10. Do not construe this as newly available under Payment Intents or as an account-wide setting for `adaptivePricing.allowed`.

New raw line 25 preserves two distinct statements: merchants are responsible for compliance with applicable price-localization laws, and Stripe requires rendering the selector when using Adaptive Pricing with Elements. Old raw line 14 says the same. Neither capture says the rendering instruction itself is imposed by law. Correct the unsupported legal characterization in source lines 13 and 18, concept wiki/concepts/stripe-currency-selector-element.md heading line 24 and source description line 64, and wiki/stripe-index.md lines 69 and 773. Preserve the must-render condition as Stripe's documented integration instruction and describe legal compliance separately.

The placement recommendations and `initCheckoutElementsSdk`/`createCurrencySelectorElement` example remain substantively the same; image URL, quote style, quickstart URL, and 'ensure' to 'make sure' changes are presentational or link changes.
substantive_changes: New before-you-begin section enumerates three currency-option display conditions at lines 17-21, including Checkout Session `adaptivePricing.allowed` and merchant-of-record settlement eligibility.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Currency Selector Element and Adaptive Pricing on this page are restricted to Elements with the Checkout Sessions API (old line 10; new line 13).

Stripe says the selector must be rendered for Adaptive Pricing with Elements, and separately says merchants are responsible for applicable price-localization law compliance (old line 14; new line 25).
Place the selector near payment details or price total, with Express Checkout placement above that element (old lines 48-51; new lines 59-62).
